objective: Confirmatory Monte Carlo on square tori with odd sides and fair visible spokes: every class's emergence (zero classes exactly 0; extensive classes growing with the area; critical classes size-independent), and the emergence of 'x or (h != h')' on five rectangular shapes and on rotated squares at sizes up to 65 compared with Pinson's prediction. Controls: two independent consistency tests agree, and bipartite tori are always consistent.
status: Closed: supported by CONTACT-CENSUS-20261022-001B-E001 (confirmatory Monte Carlo, frozen contract; controls pass; two independent tests agree on every doubly judged sample; independent replay agrees). 'x or (h != h')' matches Pinson's conformal prediction on six shapes: the two-largest-size means deviate by +0.004, +0.026, -0.010, -0.002, +0.007 bits on five rectangular shapes (sides up to 65) and +0.008 on rotated squares, each within about 1.5 standard errors (limits 1.5085, 1.9852, 1.9852, 0.6774, 1.7898 bits). The census holds: vacuum classes always consistent; parity 9.91 +- 0.10 and 15.6 +- 0.3 bits against exactly 10 and 16; swap-or-order grows from 4.29 to 11.46 bits; not-all-equal and 'x or (h != h')' are flat over sides 9-65 at distinct values (0.835 and 1.521 bits), and all 12 placements of each agree.
title: Experiment: the census measured and the conformal test
